statement: A school has $\$900$ to spend on chess sets, which cost $\$18$ each, and robotics kits, which cost $\$45$ each. The equation $18c + 45r = 900$ represents buying $c$ chess sets and $r$ robotics kits for exactly $\$900$. What is the value of $c$ when $r = 0$, and what does it represent?

choices.text: $20$; the number of robotics kits the school can buy if it buys no chess sets
choices.misconception: I divided $900$ by $45$, which gives the value of $r$ when $c = 0$, instead of the value of $c$ when $r = 0$.

choices.text: $50$; the number of robotics kits the school can buy if it buys no chess sets
choices.misconception: I computed $900 \div 18 = 50$ correctly, but I mixed up which item that number counts.

choices.text: $50$; the number of chess sets the school can buy if it buys no robotics kits
$18$; the cost, in dollars, of one chess set
choices.misconception: I read the coefficient of $c$ as the answer instead of solving for $c$ when $r = 0$.

hints: With no robotics kits, all of the money goes to chess sets. Solve for $c$, then say what that number counts.

solutions.reliable: Setting $r = 0$ gives $18c = 900$, so $c = 50$. When no robotics kits are bought, all $900$ dollars buys chess sets at $18$ dollars each, so $50$ is the number of chess sets the school can buy if it buys no robotics kits. Check: $18 \cdot 50 = 900$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
